chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Dhubyan ibn Hakim from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Nuymari from Ibn Abi Yafur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) intended to burn a group of people in their homes because they would pray in their homes and not pray in congregation. Then a blind man came to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, I am blind in vision, and sometimes I hear the call to prayer but cannot find someone to guide me to the congregation and prayer with you.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Tie a rope from your house to the mosque and attend the congregation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a blind person regarding attending congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Prophet’s initial inclination to burn the homes of those who neglected congregational prayer, a ruling later refined to prevent hardship (*raf' al-haraj*). It specifically grants the blind a practical concession—using a rope to navigate to the mosque—emphasizing that physical disability does not exempt one from the communal obligation of *salat al-jama'ah*. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing strict adherence to communal worship with compassionate legal flexibility for those with genuine impediments.
